ABSTRACT: Confinement of hydrocarbons in nanoscale pockets and pores provides tunable capability for controlling molecules in catalysts, sorbents, and membranes for reaction and separation applications. While computation of the enthalpic interactions of hydrocarbons in confined spaces has improved, understanding and predicting the entropy of confined molecules remains a challenge. Here we show, using a set of nine aluminosilicate zeolite frameworks with broad variation in pore and cavity structure, that the entropy of adsorption can be predicted as a linear combination of rotational and translational entropy. The extent of entropy lost upon adsorption is predicted using only a single material descriptor, the occupiable volume ( $ V_{occ} $). Predictive capability of confined molecular entropy permits an understanding of the relation with adsorption enthalpy, the ability to computationally screen microporous materials, and an understanding of the role of confinement on the kinetics of molecules in confined spaces.

The enthalpy and the entropy contributions to the Gibbs free energies were calculated at T = 298 K and partial pressure of 1 atm (101325 Pa). The enthalpy (H) of gas-phase pyridine and acetonitrile molecules is defined as the sum of total electronic energy ( $ E_{el} $), internal vibrational energy ( $ E_{v} $), zero-point vibrational energy (ZPVE), as well as the rotational and translational contributions to the internal energy: $ H = E_{el} + E_{v} + ZPVE + E_{R} + E_{t} $. The corresponding calculated entropies (S) includes translational, ( $ S_{t} $) vibrational, ( $ S_{v} $) and rotational ( $ S_{r} $) degrees of freedom: $ S = S_{t} + S_{v} + S_{r} $. All the considered systems are in singlet state, thus the electronic contribution to the entropy is zero. The first attempts to describe guest-induced flexibility in zeolites were done using molecular dynamics simulations. $ ^{79-82} $ Rigid zeolitic force fields were dynamically modified using transition state theory to include lattice flexibility, and the results obtained by these models were in good agreement with experimental data. $ ^{79-81,83,84} $ It was shown that framework flexibility in silicalite-1 (MFI-type framework) is responsible for the adsorption of large molecules such as isobutane and heptane with inflection behavior at high loadings, $ ^{80} $ while enhanced self-diffusivity at low loadings of short alkanes (i.e. methane and n-butane) was observed. $ ^{81} $ Framework flexibility is also crucial for aromatics adsorption on MFI zeolite, especially at high pressures. $ ^{84,85} $ While the use of rigid zeolitic models led to the underestimation of the aromatics adsorption in MFI zeolite by a factor of two, $ ^{84,85} $ the use of flexible models to simulate diffusion coefficients of various alkanes in silicalite-1 zeolite resulted in a convergence of experimental and theoretical values. $ ^{86} $ Recently by using in situ integrated differential phase contrast scanning transmission electron microscopy (iDPC-STEM) while adsorbing benzene molecules on MFI zeolite, Xiong et al. showed that the MFI structure goes through severe deformations giving another proof of guest-induced flexibility in zeolites (see Fig. 4). $ ^{87} $

2.4.4. Trapdoor. Traditional diﬀusion models primarily consider two types of interactions: those between guest molecules (guest–guest) and those between guest molecules and the zeolite framework (guest–host). However, when cations are present in the zeolite structure, a third interaction—involving guest molecules, the framework, and cations (guest–host-cation)—must also be accounted for. A striking example of such ternary interactions is the well-known ‘‘molecular trapdoor’’. This phenomenon, also referred to as the ‘‘gating effect’’, describes a unique molecular sieving mechanism in certain zeolites and related porous materi- als. Here, extra-framework cations function as dynamic gate- keepers at pore apertures, selectively controlling molecular diffusion to achieve highly discriminative adsorption and separation.9,147,187 To date, ‘‘trapdoor’’ has been observed in several zeolites, including RHO (DNL-6),188–190 CHA (SAPO-34, SSZ-13),147,191,192 MWF (ZSM-25),149,193 HEU (Clinoptilolite),194

descriptor_candidates.name: pore_confinement_ratio
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss upon adsorption scales with the ratio of molecular volume to the cube of the largest pore diameter: frameworks whose largest free-sphere diameter cubed barely exceeds the molecular volume confine translational/rotational motion most strongly, giving the largest S_ads/S_gas deficit. Including this ratio as a nonlinear network input should reduce MAE of entropy loss/R relative to the 14-input baseline.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from confinement entropy literature (E01, E03): a single material descriptor capturing occupiable volume predicts entropy loss because tighter confinement freezes more degrees of freedom. This descriptor re-expresses that mechanism as a molecule-size-to-pore-dimension ratio, distinguishing tight one-dimensional channels (small lsd_p) from large cavities (FAU-like).
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If cross-validated MAE of entropy loss/R with this descriptor added does not improve (or degrades) versus the full 14-input baseline, or if the ratio is uncorrelated with entropy loss across frameworks (TON vs FAU contrast in E01), the hypothesis is rejected.

descriptor_candidates.name: shape_asymmetry_confinement
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Molecular shape anisotropy (PMI3/PMI1) interacting with the fit between molecular dimension (GeDi) and the smallest pore diameter (lsd_f) determines rotational entropy loss: rod-like molecules entering tight windows lose rotational entropy most, while compact molecules in spacious cages lose least. Adding this shape-fit term should reduce MAE of entropy loss/R.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from E01 (rotational vs translational entropy fractions differ by framework and molecule shape) and E05 (shape selectivity depends on matching between molecular bulkiness and pore windows). Molecular moments of inertia encode rod/disc/sphere geometry; GeDi vs lsd_f encodes window-entry friction.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If the network residual analysis shows this descriptor adds no predictive information (MAE change within noise of cross-validation variance), or if entropy loss for anisotropic molecules in tubular pores (e.g., alkanes in TON) is not systematically larger than for compact molecules in FAU as this term predicts, reject.

descriptor_candidates.name: density_weighted_surface_cage_index
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss combines two independent mechanisms: (i) high framework density with large accessible surface per framework volume creates many wall-contact configurations that suppress translational entropy, and (ii) small plane-of-best-fit thickness (PBF) relative to molecular span indicates planar confinement that suppresses rotation. Adding this composite index should reduce MAE of entropy loss/R beyond either term alone.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference: E01 shows absolute entropy loss is framework-specific (TON largest, FAU smallest), implying both material packing (density, ASA/Vol) and molecular-fitting geometry (PBF, SPAN) matter. E06 indicates independent suppression of translational and rotational modes, motivating a composite rather than a single descriptor.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If ablation shows removing this descriptor from the 15-input network leaves MAE of entropy loss/R statistically unchanged, or if the two additive mechanisms cannot be separated (the composite performs no better than either factor alone), the two-mechanism hypothesis is falsified.

descriptor_candidates.name: volumetric_packing_fraction
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss (S_gas - S_ads)/R increases monotonically with the fraction of the largest free-sphere volume occupied by the molecule: when the molecular volume fills a substantial part of the largest sphere that fits the pore, translational freedom is nearly frozen and entropy loss approaches the full three-translational-degree limit; when the fraction is small (large cavities), loss is minimal. Adding this single packing fraction as a 15th network input should reduce the cross-validated MAE of entropy loss/R below the 14-input baseline.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from E01 and E03: E01 reports framework-dependent absolute entropy loss (TON largest, FAU smallest), and E03 shows a single material volume descriptor (occupiable volume) largely predicts confined entropy. Here the analogous information is re-expressed as a molecule-to-pore volumetric filling ratio, which directly bounds the number of distinguishable translational configurations. Source evidence establishes the volume-confinement relation; the specific packing-fraction form with lsd_p and molecular Vol is an inferred new combination, not a verified literature relation.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If adding this descriptor leaves the cross-validated MAE of entropy loss/R unchanged or worse than the 14-input baseline (marginal improvement <= 0), or if residual analysis shows the network assigns it negligible weight while E01's TON-vs-FAU contrast is already captured by existing inputs, the packing-fraction mechanism hypothesis is falsified. It is also falsified if entropy loss correlates negatively with the fraction across frameworks, contradicting monotonic confinement.

descriptor_candidates.name: planarity_window_compression
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Disc-like (planar) molecules, identified by a large intermediate-to-minimum moment ratio PMI2/PMI1, suffer disproportionately larger rotational entropy loss in frameworks whose smallest free-sphere diameter (lsd_f) is much smaller than their largest free-sphere diameter (lsd_p), i.e., in window-cage or channel-cage topologies where passage through tight windows forces alignment while cages permit free rotation. The product of molecular planarity and window-to-cage compression should therefore correlate positively with entropy loss/R and improve MAE beyond the retained shape-asymmetry term, which encodes rod-like anisotropy (PMI3/PMI1) instead.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from E01 (rotational entropy fraction varies systematically with molecule shape and framework) and E05 (shape selectivity arises from geometric matching between molecular bulk and pore windows, giving distinct adsorption states for closely related isomers). E09's discussion of symmetry-dependent rotational motion under confinement supports a shape-specific rotational mechanism. This descriptor is deliberately orthogonal to the retained PMI3/PMI1 term: it probes the second principal inertia and the lsd_f/lsd_p window-cage contrast rather than the long-axis ratio and GeDi/lsd_f fit.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Falsified if cross-validation shows no MAE improvement of entropy loss/R over the 15-input model that already contains the retained shape_asymmetry_confinement term (marginal improvement <= 0), or if partial dependence of entropy loss on PMI2/PMI1 is flat after controlling for the retained term, indicating planarity-window compression carries no independent rotational-entropy information.

descriptor_candidates.name: contact_area_adsorption_state_index
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss decreases with the number of energetically equivalent adsorption states: molecules with high specific surface (LabuteASA/Vol, more wall-contact orientations) adsorbed in frameworks with roomy pore networks per unit of accessible surface (AV/ASA, many distinguishable placements) retain more gas-phase entropy. This term should contribute negatively to predicted entropy loss/R and reduce MAE, capturing a configurational-degeneracy mechanism distinct from the geometric confinement ratios already present.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from E01 (surface entropy never exceeds gas entropy, but the deficit varies by framework, implying framework-dependent configurational degeneracy) and E06 (translational and rotational modes are suppressed by distinct mechanisms and reduced independently, motivating a separate surface-contact/degeneracy channel). E04's pore-size-dependent reorganization of confined structures further supports a contact-geometry-dependent entropic contribution. Density, ASA, and AV enter on their native source scales without assigned physical units; the ratio AV/ASA is used only dimensionlessly.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Falsified if the descriptor's cross-validated marginal MAE improvement on entropy loss/R is zero or negative, or if the learned network response to this term is non-monotonic/unstable across folds (sign flips), indicating no robust configurational-degeneracy effect. A positive response of entropy loss (instead of the hypothesized negative one) would also falsify the stated mechanism.

descriptor_candidates.name: elongation_pore_asphericity
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss/R grows with the product of molecular elongation (SPAN/PBF: how rod-like the molecule is relative to its thickness) and framework asphericity (lsd_p/lsd_f: contrast between largest cavity and smallest window). Rod-like molecules in window-cage frameworks must align to pass windows and stay aligned in channels, suppressing rotation maximally; spherical molecules in cage-only frameworks lose least. Adding this 16th input should reduce cross-validated MAE of entropy loss/R below the current 15-input baseline.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference: E01 shows TON (1D channel) gives the largest entropy loss and FAU (large cages) the smallest, suggesting channel-vs-cage topology modulates rotational suppression; E05 shows window matching dictates distinct adsorption states. SPAN/PBF is a molecular-shape axis orthogonal to the retained PMI3/PMI1 term (which mixes anisotropy with GeDi/lsd_f fit), and lsd_p/lsd_f is a topology contrast not yet used in any retained descriptor.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Rejected if cross-validated marginal MAE improvement on entropy loss/R is <= 0 versus the 15-input baseline, or if partial dependence on SPAN/PBF is flat after controlling for shape_asymmetry_confinement, showing no independent elongation mechanism.

descriptor_candidates.name: mass_surface_freedom_index
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Translational entropy loss scales with molecular mass per contact area (MW/LabuteASA, heavier molecules have larger Sackur-Tetrode translational entropy to lose per unit wall interaction) modulated by the framework's surface packing intensity sqrt(ASA/Vol): dense, high-surface frameworks freeze translation more. The product should correlate positively with entropy loss/R and reduce MAE by giving the network an explicit mass-normalized contact-strength channel absent from the retained geometric ratios.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference: E01 derives translational entropy from the Sackur-Tetrode equation, which depends explicitly on mass, implying mass-normalized descriptors carry translational-entropy information the network can exploit; E06 shows translational and rotational modes are suppressed independently, motivating a dedicated translational channel distinct from the retained rotational/shape terms. MW/LabuteASA and ASA/Vol are dimensionless or scale-free ratios used only as network inputs.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Falsified if marginal MAE improvement <= 0 in cross-validation, or if the learned response is non-monotonic/sign-flipped across folds, or if residuals show no improvement for heavy adsorbates (large MW/LabuteASA) where the translational mechanism predicts the largest gains.

This term should reduce MAE of entropy loss/R by encoding a mechanism (orientation-specific wall commensuration) distinct from confinement ratios and configurational degeneracy already present.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference: E09 shows molecular symmetry affects confined dynamics (rotational freedom differs among near-isomers of identical size and mass), implying PMI asymmetry beyond the long/short ratio carries independent entropy information; E08 shows guest-induced framework flexibility relates to framework density and accessible volume, motivating the density*AV/Vol compactness factor. Density is used only on its native source scale, no unverified units assigned.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: Falsified if cross-validated MAE of entropy loss/R does not improve (marginal improvement <= 0), or if ablating the PMI3-PMI2 asymmetry factor leaves performance unchanged (indicating the retained PMI3/PMI1 term already captures all shape information), or if partial dependence on density*AV/Vol is flat after controlling for existing inputs.

candidates.name: mass_surface_freedom_index
candidates.hypothesis: Translational entropy loss scales with molecular mass per contact area (MW/LabuteASA, heavier molecules have larger Sackur-Tetrode translational entropy to lose per unit wall interaction) modulated by the framework's surface packing intensity sqrt(ASA/Vol): dense, high-surface frameworks freeze translation more. The product should correlate positively with entropy loss/R and reduce MAE by giving the network an explicit mass-normalized contact-strength channel absent from the retained geometric ratios.
candidates.rationale: Inference: E01 derives translational entropy from the Sackur-Tetrode equation, which depends explicitly on mass, implying mass-normalized descriptors carry translational-entropy information the network can exploit; E06 shows translational and rotational modes are suppressed independently, motivating a dedicated translational channel distinct from the retained rotational/shape terms. MW/LabuteASA and ASA/Vol are dimensionless or scale-free ratios used only as network inputs.
candidates.falsification_criteria: Falsified if marginal MAE improvement <= 0 in cross-validation, or if the learned response is non-monotonic/sign-flipped across folds, or if residuals show no improvement for heavy adsorbates (large MW/LabuteASA) where the translational mechanism predicts the largest gains.

candidates.name: inertia_heterogeneity_density
candidates.hypothesis: Molecular inertia heterogeneity (|PMI3-PMI2|/PMI2: asymmetry between the two largest principal moments, distinguishing rods from discs beyond the retained PMI3/PMI1 ratio) combined with framework guest-accessible compactness (density * AV/Vol, how much accessible pore volume exists per unit framework mass) jointly control rotational-vibrational entropy redistribution: asymmetric molecules in compact frameworks lose the most entropy because few orientations are commensurate with the walls. This term should reduce MAE of entropy loss/R by encoding a mechanism (orientation-specific wall commensuration) distinct from confinement ratios and configurational degeneracy already present.
candidates.rationale: Inference: E09 shows molecular symmetry affects confined dynamics (rotational freedom differs among near-isomers of identical size and mass), implying PMI asymmetry beyond the long/short ratio carries independent entropy information; E08 shows guest-induced framework flexibility relates to framework density and accessible volume, motivating the density*AV/Vol compactness factor. Density is used only on its native source scale, no unverified units assigned.
candidates.falsification_criteria: Falsified if cross-validated MAE of entropy loss/R does not improve (marginal improvement <= 0), or if ablating the PMI3-PMI2 asymmetry factor leaves performance unchanged (indicating the retained PMI3/PMI1 term already captures all shape information), or if partial dependence on density*AV/Vol is flat after controlling for existing inputs.

interpretation: Replicates vary LLM proposals on one fixed split, not independent datasets. Novelty is unverified.

retained.name: shape_asymmetry_confinement
retained.hypothesis: Molecular shape anisotropy (PMI3/PMI1) interacting with the fit between molecular dimension (GeDi) and the smallest pore diameter (lsd_f) determines rotational entropy loss: rod-like molecules entering tight windows lose rotational entropy most, while compact molecules in spacious cages lose least. Adding this shape-fit term should reduce MAE of entropy loss/R.

retained.name: contact_area_adsorption_state_index
retained.hypothesis: Entropy loss decreases with the number of energetically equivalent adsorption states: molecules with high specific surface (LabuteASA/Vol, more wall-contact orientations) adsorbed in frameworks with roomy pore networks per unit of accessible surface (AV/ASA, many distinguishable placements) retain more gas-phase entropy. This term should contribute negatively to predicted entropy loss/R and reduce MAE, capturing a configurational-degeneracy mechanism distinct from the geometric confinement ratios already present.
